title: Intraoperative Evaluation of Circulation, Metabolism and Body Composition (INTRICATE Study)
summary:
Background: During long surgeries, there can be significant changes in a patient's blood circulation and metabolism. These changes often require treatments to stabilize blood pressure and manage stress and inflammation in the body. However, the effects of these surgeries on body composition (like muscle and fat) and metabolism are not well understood. Additionally, we know little about how a person’s body composition might influence the effectiveness of anesthesia and related drugs.

Aims:

This study aims to understand how changes in blood circulation are related to metabolism in adults undergoing major surgery. It will look at how large and small blood vessels function during surgery, the treatments given, and how these factors relate to changes in blood flow, energy use, and body composition before and after surgery.

Another goal is to investigate how body composition affects the use and outcomes of anesthesia-related drugs, including painkillers, sedatives, and muscle relaxants.

Study Design: This study will involve around 100 adult patients who are undergoing planned surgeries expected to last more than three hours. Starting in October 2024, the study will enroll patients over a 12-month period. During surgery, researchers will closely monitor the patients' blood circulation, metabolism, body composition, and drug use. After surgery, patients will continue to be observed during their hospital stay. To gather comprehensive data, various techniques will be used, including measuring energy use, analyzing body composition, examining the quadriceps muscle, monitoring blood oxygen levels, and conducting brain activity tests and blood gas analyses.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Given informed consent
2.	Adult patients (≥ 18 years)
3.	Elective major surgery with anticipated duration of > 180 minutes
4.	Patients receiving central venous and arterial access as per clinical routine
Exclusion criteria:
•	Patients < 18 years, pregnant or lactating patients 
•	Patients unable to consent or follow instructions from medical team (cognitive, psychiatric, or severe language barriers)
•	Medical conditions, surgical and anesthesia-related procedures preventing the intraoperative use of the planned medical devices 
•	Propofol allergy as contraindication for total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA)
•	Enrolment in an industry sponsored randomized trial within the last 30 days (co-enrolment in academic randomized trials will be considered on a case-by-case basis)
